root_cause_label: ILP variables not declared as binary/integer and incorrect budget constraint formulation yields wrong NPV (358.00 vs 361.00)
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent wrote an ILP model that failed to declare variables as binary/integer (producing the 'No integer variables' CBC warning) and had incorrect budget constraint logic, yielding NPV=358.00 instead of the correct 361.00, and then accepted the wrong result without investigating the discrepancy between the LP relaxation value (361) and final output (358).
t_err_evidence: create /app/investment_problem.py with continuous (non-integer) variables, so the ILP is mis-modeled
t_commit_evidence: Step 5: The script runs and outputs 'Optimization complete. Results saved to /app/ilp_output.txt' after producing an LP-only solution of 361 vs a final MIP result of 358; the agent proceeds directly to read the output file rather than investigating the 'No integer variables' warning or the LP/MIP value discrepancy.
trigger_explanation: The agent formulated the ILP correctly at a high level (choosing A, deferring B, choosing C) but the code generation produced a model that failed to declare decision variables as binary integers and had an incorrect budget constraint, causing the solver to skip the MIP phase entirely and report a wrong feasible value.
